name: Generic provider modem (the box the internet service arrives in)
build: blender -b --factory-startup --python source/build_modem_generic.py, then glTF-Transform dedup → weld → meshopt
units: metres; origin at the centre of the base; front faces +Z in three.js
colour_note: light grey, deliberately unlike the school's own charcoal equipment: in a film a teacher must be able to see at a glance which box is theirs and which belongs to the provider.

anchors.port_lan: LAN port — the cable to the router's WAN (outward normal +Z)
anchors.port_line: LINE port — the provider's own line (generic: a smaller socket; real CPEs differ by technology)
anchors.led_link: LINK — the provider line is synchronised
anchors.led_internet: INTERNET — the provider's service is up
anchors.led_lan: LAN — a device is connected on the Ethernet side

behaviour: generic; see ../../../README.md § LED states. The split that matters: LINK and INTERNET describe the UPSTREAM side, LAN describes the cable to the router. A film can therefore show 'the physical link to the router is down' while the provider's service is perfectly healthy — which is the commonest real case and the one a teacher must not confuse with an outage.

provenance.origin: original work, authored for OE by the explainer engine (procedural Blender script)
provenance.creator: OE Support explainer engine
provenance.license: OE-owned; no third-party geometry, textures or trademarks. No provider's branding: the printed word is 'PROVIDER'.
